title: Universal inversion below the local-function stretch exponent
summary: Decide whether every fixed local predicate admits efficient inversion below Applebaum's stated output-length exponent.

formal_statement.body: For every fixed $d$-local Boolean predicate $P$, does there exist a constant $\varepsilon>0$ and an efficient algorithm that inverts a random member of the Goldreich collection $F_{P,n,m}$ with nonnegligible success when $$m=n^{\lfloor 2d/3\rfloor/2-\varepsilon}?$$ Give such an inverter uniformly for every fixed $P$, or prove an admissible predicate family prevents efficient inversion in the stated model.

scope.domain: Random local functions and Goldreich one-way-function candidates
assumptions: P is a fixed d-local Boolean predicate
F_(P,n,m) is sampled from the Goldreich random-neighborhood collection
scope.unresolved_remainder: Known attacks, conditional search-to-decision reductions, and results for special predicates do not provide an efficient inverter for every fixed d-local predicate at the stated exponent and do not refute the universal statement.

provenance.note: The 2022 TIT paper quotes the open question from Applebaum and preserves its predicate quantifier and output exponent.

progress.summary: The TIT source restates the universal question while studying concrete XOR-AND predicates.
A universal constant-arity search-to-decision reduction gives inversion conditional on an efficient distinguisher, but its output blowup does not reach Applebaum's target exponent.
